key_insight: The paper argues that major milestones (exemplified by AlphaGo) should be interpreted as starting points for long-term, cumulative change — understanding AI requires a strategic, long-game view rather than treating breakthroughs as isolated events.
problem_solved: Addresses the lack of a systematic, long-range perspective on how milestone systems reshape research directions, evaluation practices and deployment priorities across the following decade.
method: Qualitative historical review of landmark events in AI (e.g., AlphaGo) and their downstream effects on research agendas.
Synthesis of observed trends and pathways linking breakthroughs to subsequent methodological, engineering and policy changes.
Derivation of strategic lessons and suggested priorities for sustaining and governing long-term AI progress.
impact: Helps AI/ML practitioners and research managers plan research agendas, design evaluation frameworks and anticipate cascading technical and societal effects from major advances; encourages shifting focus from one-off wins to durable, cumulative progress.
visual_elements: Timeline of AI milestones (AlphaGo → key developments over the next decade) showing causality arrows to subsequent research areas.
Sankey/flow diagram mapping a milestone to research, engineering, deployment and policy branches to illustrate cascading effects.
Circular 'long-game' strategy diagram (iterate: discovery → scale → evaluate → govern) to show sustained progress cycles.
Icon set: Go board (milestone), lightbulb (innovation), gears (engineering), shield/scale (governance/evaluation)
